description:
HTR-10 uses a helical-coil once-through modular steam generator with helium on the shell side. The current secondary is a working and tested Rankine cycle but with hard-fixed live steam pressure, so there is no sliding-pressure or drum dynamics.

SCOPE: three-zone moving-boundary once-through SG (subcooled, evaporating, superheated) with helical-coil heat-transfer and pressure-drop correlations, plus SG inventory so that steam pressure becomes a computed variable rather than a constant.

REUSE: the LMTD and NTU algebra already exists in crates/outram-park-fork-dwsim-libs. The zone tracking and the helical correlations do not.

This is the real remaining content of the existing bead op-wqk.9.3 — the other defects that bead lists (simplified IHX duty, fixed secondary mass flow, no real turbine expansion, no condenser balance) are recorded in the scoping doc as ALREADY FIXED AND TESTED. Only fixed steam pressure remains true.
title: HTR-10: helical-coil once-through steam generator with sliding steam pressure

description:
## The gap

There is no stage-resolved steam turbine model anywhere in the workspace. Every
turbine that exists today is lumped:

- `tampines-steam-tables/src/steam_turbine_equations/` contains exactly two
  things, converging-diverging nozzle / choked-flow relations and the
  three-phase generator equations. There is no turbine stage model.
- `ThreePhaseElectricGeneratorTurbine` works, but it is a single torque balance
  advancing one rotor speed. It has no internal stations.
- `tampines::components::Turbine` carries an inlet state and an adiabatic
  efficiency, and its `expand_to` is unimplemented, so it produces no shaft
  speed at all.
- `outram-park-digital-twin-engine/src/components/turbine.rs` does talk about
  degree of reaction and per-stage blade angles, but that is the renderer. Its
  `StageAngles` are documented as placeholders driving blade geometry on
  screen, not a flow solve.

So the vocabulary of staging exists only in the drawing layer, and the physics
underneath it is a single lumped expansion.

## What to build

A mean-flow, stage-by-stage steam turbine model in `tampines-steam-tables`,
built on the crate's existing 1D homogeneous-equilibrium machinery, with **one
control volume per stage**.

### Control volumes

One `TampinesSteamTableCV` per stage, carrying that stage's steam state. The
crate already has what this needs:

- `advance_timestep(&CvMassEnthalpyChanges)` conserves mass and energy over a
  step, then recovers pressure by solving `v(p, h_new) = v_new` with regula
  falsi and rebuilds the volume from `(p, h_new)`. That is the marching scheme.
- `expand_isentropically(new_p)` and `expand_with_work_extensive(...)` give the
  ideal expansion and the work-extracting one.
- The equilibrium flashes (`ph_flash_eqm`, `ps_flash_eqm`) are the HEM closure,
  and they already carry the wet-steam behaviour a low-pressure stage needs.
- `interfaces/checked/control_volume.rs` gives bounds-checked constructors, so
  stage states can be built without inheriting the raw flash panics.

Stages chain inlet to exhaust, each one's outlet feeding the next one's inlet.

### Velocity triangles, per stage

Each stage gets a real velocity triangle at the mean radius: blade speed from
shaft speed and mean radius, absolute and relative velocities, and flow angles
at rotor inlet and outlet. The triangle is what connects the thermodynamic
state in the control volume to the work actually extracted, rather than an
assumed stage efficiency.

### Impulse and reaction handled differently

This is the part that matters and it is deliberate:

- **Impulse stages** get their work from the **velocity triangles**. Momentum
  change of the steam turning through the rotor gives the tangential force, and
  the Euler work follows from that directly.
- **Reaction stages** get their work from **simplified lift equations** on the
  blade rows, treating the row as an aerofoil cascade rather than a pure
  deflector.

A real machine mixes the two, impulse at the high-pressure admission end and
reaction towards the low-pressure exhaust, so the model needs both and needs to
know which applies where.

## Related existing work

The quasi-1D nozzle relations in
`steam_turbine_equations/converging_diverging_nozzles/differential_nozzle_equations.rs`
already march pressure through an area change using the area-Mach influence
coefficient, and go singular at the throat. Worth reusing for the nozzle
row rather than rewriting, and worth reading before choosing the stage
marching scheme.

The homogeneous-equilibrium choked-flow work is already validated against
Moody, Zaloudek and Marviken, so the HEM closure is not being introduced cold.

## Open questions

- Whether the stage marching is steady (solve the chain once per call) or
  transient (`advance_timestep` per stage per timestep). The transient path is
  what the control volume was built for, but a turbine is usually much faster
  than the plant transient around it.
- How the degree of reaction is supplied per stage. Given as geometry, or
  derived from the velocity triangle.
- Where moisture in the last stages feeds back, if at all. HEM assumes
  equilibrium, so it will not capture supersaturation or droplet lag.

## Acceptance

- A multi-stage machine runs inlet to exhaust and conserves mass and energy
  across the chain.
- Total work matches a lumped isentropic expansion times a sensible efficiency,
  within a stated tolerance, so the stage model is not silently wrong.
- Impulse and reaction stages are demonstrably taking different paths to work,
  not the same formula behind two names.

---

Tracked on GitHub as gh:#164 — https://github.com/theodoreOnzGit/outram-park-backend/issues/164

notes.content: First cut landed on develop: ba7eca5e (model) + a5c09db5 (v0.2.9 docs). Design changed from the original write-up per maintainer direction: no stage is purely impulse or reaction. Every stage carries both, solved in two parts -- impulse redirection first (Euler on the velocity triangle), then reaction from the rotor pressure drop via cascade lift on the velocity increment dw = sqrt(w2^2 + 2 dh_rotor) - w2. Zero rotor drop gives zero reaction work, reducing exactly to the classical impulse stage; asserted. 14 tests + 1 ignored diagnostic; suite 996 passed / 0 failed / 14 ignored. Still open: no published stage-by-stage validation case, mean-line only, stage pressures not solved from a mass-flow match, lift coefficient is an input rather than derived from geometry. Progress detail: gh:#164 comment 5599365525.

title: tampines-steam-tables: mean-flow stage-by-stage steam turbine model (one HEM control volume per stage)
